answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven duplication. Like a single ember kept alive on a knoll above a sprawling nebula of anonymous accounts, one verified agent stands out because faking a thousand copies would mean funding a thousand stakes. Honest agents earn fees back over time, while an attacker must pay real capital per fake identity, making large-scale forgery expensive and easy to spot when stakes cluster.
